assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing is the clearest game-changer on the list: a chemical solution (reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis on clustered surfaces, and emulsion/pyrosequencing approaches) that cut the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude and reshaped biology and medicine. The core is molecular chemistry and single-molecule detection, so it fits Chemistry rather than being only a tool of biology.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa chemistry traces to Balasubramanian and Klenerman, and the first commercial massively parallel platform came from Rothberg's 454 work. Clustering and reversible-terminator chemistry involved several others (for example Jingyue Ju, Pascal Mayer), so a three-person cap forces a hard choice, and I rank this configuration as the most defensible rather than certain.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of routine, independent, global use with enormous demonstrated consequences. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to credit the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry alone or both competing platforms is unresolved.
Credit among Illumina/Solexa contributors beyond the two academic founders is contested and I have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity is a genuinely new therapeutic modality, with a chemical principle (heterobifunctional molecules and molecular glues recruiting E3 ligases) that has already produced clinical candidates. It is new, simple in concept, and already has real consequences.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the molecular-glue degraders. Ciulli and Gray made major later contributions and Sakamoto did the first experiments, so the three-person limit leaves real unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Maturity is good but not complete: many degraders are in late clinical trials, yet approval-level proof is still developing, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical validation of PROTACs is not yet complete.
Attribution among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others is disputed and could favour a different trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made first-principles dynamics of condensed phases and reactions practical, and it underlies ab initio simulation of water, solids and reactive chemistry. Theory here connects quantitatively to experiment, which is the standard I apply.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is exceptionally clean: the 1985 paper by two authors. Parrinello's later work on metadynamics and machine-learned potentials strengthens his case but should not dilute the Car-Parrinello credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with four decades of independent use and development. The prize is arguably long overdue, with the caveat that the 2013 multiscale prize and 1998 DFT prize already honoured neighbouring theory.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier computational chemistry prizes may reduce the committee's appetite.
Candidate Parrinello also appears on other computational entries; I have treated this one on its own merits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a simple, general, widely used method for making arylamines and is routine in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It extends the logic of the 2010 cross-coupling prize in a distinct and highly consequential direction.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-based catalytic systems and are the natural pair; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor that complicates priority but does not support a third laureate as strongly.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed, with extensive industrial use.
uncertainties: The 2010 cross-coupling prize may be seen as having already covered this area.
Priority relative to Kosugi's earlier work is a point on which I rely on general knowledge, unverified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory gave a quantitative, conceptual resolution of how proteins fold, and Fersht's protein engineering and phi-value analysis provide the matching experimental mapping. This is the kind of theory tied to experiment that I value.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes with Bryngelson and Onuchic carried the theory, Fersht the experiments, and Dill the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model line. A fair prize needs a balanced theory-plus-experiment trio, but the priority among theorists is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and have been confirmed by many experiments and simulations. Recognition is timely, though the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design touched on neighbouring ground.
uncertainties: Dill's and Bryngelson's contributions are excluded by the cap and may be judged equal to Onuchic's.
Possible perception of overlap with the 2024 protein prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single nucleotides without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminase chemistry on DNA, and has moved quickly into clinical use. It is original, clear in concept and already consequential.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive contributions to both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors as trainees, and Nishida and Kondo reported a parallel cytidine editor. A single-laureate configuration is cleanest, though it leaves the parallel work unrecognised.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with early clinical proof, but long-term safety and efficacy data are limited, and CRISPR was already honoured in 2020.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would consider genome-editing chemistry as recognised by the 2020 prize.
Credit for the independent Nishida and Kondo work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached high efficiencies at remarkable speed, and the discovery opened a new class of solution-processed semiconductors. It is clearly a game-changer in terms of science activity, with consequences mostly still ahead.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cells, Park the first solid-state cells with high stability and efficiency, and Snaith the thin-film and meso-superstructured devices. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel all have strong claims, making allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Premature in one respect: long-term stability and commercial deployment are not demonstrated, so real-world consequences are not yet shown.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercialisation remain unresolved.
Attribution is highly contested among at least six credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing translated single-molecule ionic-current detection into direct electrical reading of DNA and RNA, with consequences visible in portable sequencers. It is simple in principle and has real, demonstrated consequences.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the concept in 1996; Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled DNA translocation that made sequencing practical. Branton is deceased, which constrains the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough to be in wide use, though accuracy continues to evolve, and the sequencing field overlaps with the stronger B011 candidate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the massively parallel sequencing candidate may mean only one sequencing prize is likely.
My recollection of Branton's status and exact priority relationships is not independently verified.
